sentences.text: registered at Police Station Mohan Nagar, District Durg (C.G.), for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 377 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that the prosecutrix got acquainted with the applicant through a matrimonial site 'jeevansathi.com' on 11.09.2022.
After talking with the prosecutrix, the applicant came to Surya Palace Durg to meet her.
On 12.09.2022 some talks with respect to the marriage proposal took place in presence of her mother.
On 13.09.2022 at 2.00 p.m. both their families have consented to their marriage and they will get married very soon.

The applicant without her consent forcefully had physical relationship with her, on 12.04.2023 when they have gone to Manali, there also he had physical relationship with her, on 19.04.2023 they stayed at Gulmohar Hotel at Gwalior where the applicant booked the room and there also he ravished her and on 20.04.2023 at around 12.00 p.m., he committed unnatural sex with her and have bitten her, on her chest, thigh and face.
On 21.04.2023, the prosecutrix returned back to her house situated at Durg and thereafter, the applicant switched off his phone.
On 03.05.2023, the applicant refused to marry her on the ground that the prosecutrix belongs to low caste and have threatened to kill her on this the prosecutrix lodged the FIR against the applicant.

3. It has been argued by Ms. Fouzia Mirza, learned Senior Advocate, assisted by Ms. Smita Jha,
learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and admittedly the prosecutrix is a major girl and she was a consenting party.

She further argued that the applicant acquainted with the prosecutrix to a matrimonial site 'jeevansathi.com', wherein her profile she has mention that she is married and divorce is under process similarly the applicant has also mentioned in his profile that he is married awaiting divorce.

It Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21278 is further submitted by the learned Senior Advocate that the applicant and the prosecutrix are in relationship since 1 year and were aware of the matrimonial status.
The prosecutrix was pressurizing the applicant to marry her as she has received the divorce decree on mutual consent and the applicant still awaiting divorce.
The prosecutrix forced the applicant to marry her surreptitiously at a Mandir to which he refused.
Thereafter, prosecutrix lodged the FIR against the applicant.
She also submitted that from perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., it transpires that she was a consenting party.

It is further argued by the learned Senior Advocate for the applicant that the applicant has no previous criminal antecedents and he is in jail since 02.06.2023 and the conclusion of the trial is likely to take quite long time.
Therefore, he prays for grant of regular bail to the applicant.
4. On the other hand, learned Deputy Advocate General appearing for the State/non-applicant would oppose the bail application.
5. I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and the prosecutrix is a major girl and she was capable of giving her consent and the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., she states that she is Manish Sharma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137205439/

sentences.text: a consenting party and further that the conclusion of the trial may take some more time, this Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail in this case.

7. Let the applicant-Manish Sharma involved in Crime No. 198/2023 Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21278 registered at Police Station Mohan Nagar, District Durg, for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 377 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, be released on bail on him furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

entities.text: Police Station Mohan Nagar, District Durg
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21278 statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

8. However, this Court hope and trust that the trial Court shall make an earnest endeavour to conclude the trial within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order, if there is no legal impediment.
9. Office is directed to send a certified copy of this order to the trial Court for necessary information and compliance within one week from today.

- Sd/-
 (Ramesh Sinha)
